newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace news halts Rome fashion show preparations.
newsitem.headline: Versace news halts Rome fashion show preparations.

text.p: The bustle and euphoria of preparing for a glamorous fashion gala suddenly turned to tears and confusion in Rome on Tuesday as family, friends and models heard fashion designer Gianni Versace had been murdered.

Versace's sister Donatella and brother Santo, who had been waiting for Gianni to join them in Rome on Wednesday, were rushed by police through a throng of reporters, photographers and fans crowded outside a central hotel.
Police said they had left the city to fly to Miami Beach where the 50-year-old designer was shot in the head by an unknown assailant on the doorstep of his mansion.
Giuseppe Modanese, vice-chairman of Italy's National Chamber of Fashion, said the family was sure his name would live on.
"What they told me is: 'Gianni is not dead'," he said.
Bewildered and teary models stopped their fittings as organisers decided to indefinitely postpone Wednesday's gala finale to Rome's "alta moda" (haute couture) week on the famous Spanish Steps.
"Right now, I don't feel like going on...I just can't believe it," stammered Tracy Jo, one of Versace's models, as she walked in a daze.
"Everyone is crying up there, they are all in shock," another dark-haired model, wearing sunglasses, said as she was ushered through the crowd.
Italian designers wandered aimlessly, unsure whether to cancel their presentations or adhere to the show business adage "the show must go on".
"My show has involved hundreds of people. It wouldn't be right to them to cancel, but...," stopped short Italian designer Renato Balestra. "I can only think that if Gianni were here, he'd say do it."
Rocco Barocco said he would like to present his collection on Wednesday afternoon as planned, as a tribute to Versace, but would agree to whatever the Fashion Chamber decided.
Balestra said he could not think of a reason for the murder of the original and flamboyant artist.
"He was such a simple person, well-liked. No one could have ever suspected such a thing," he said.
Girls who had gathered outside the hotel to catch a glimpse of the famous models now turned away in dismay, reluctant to approach the sombre scene.
"I'm very upset. I really liked him. He was the only designer that I thought tried to understand people," said Simona Ieraci, 17.
Paolo Franzese, manager of one of the five Versace boutiques of Rome's historic centre said the shops would probably organise a commemoration for the designer.
In a sign of mouring, Versace boutiques in Milan drew the shutters early on Tuesday night.
"All I can express at the moment is utter shock," Franzese said. "It is certainly a great loss for fashion and for the cultural world in general."
